trickyParts: Ordering the two fake clones without timers: the fake `jj git clone` gates the FIRST clone on the second clone's invocation (a Promise.withResolvers gate) so both callers have passed the already-cloned check and hold a temporary destination before either returns — otherwise fs-op completion order could let caller A rename before caller B reached existsSync(repoCloneDir), and B would skip cloning (one clone, no collision). The second clone then waits on `whenPathExists(path.dirname(repoCloneDir), <repoCloneDir>/.jj)`, an fs.watch on the clone's parent re-checked after arming; Bun 1.3.14 fs.watch detected the rename 300/300 in a standalone probe.

Negative control (Acceptance 3b): making `if ((code === "ENOTEMPTY" || code === "EEXIST") && existsSync(jjDir)) return;` unreachable makes the new test fail with ENOTEMPTY on the second caller's rename — quoted in PR #1014's body; the change was reverted before commit and the pushed head carries the original line.

The bookmark legion/LEGION-55 was provisioned pointing at the undescribed working copy (which also holds the daemon-written .omp/config.yml); commits were carved out with `jj split <path>` and the bookmark moved to the described commit with `-r @- --allow-backwards` so .omp/config.yml is never pushed.
deviations: The architect's plan said the second clone waits until `.jj` exists at the final path; the test additionally holds the first clone until the second has been invoked, so exactly two clones run deterministically. No product code changed; no daemon fixture changed.
